37	/// after-help and the no-benches listing so the two stay in sync.
38	const COMMANDS_HELP: &str = concat!(
39	    "Commands:\n",
40	    "  all        run every registered bench\n",
41	    "  qualify-environment\n",
42	    "             is this machine fit to measure on? Respawns this binary\n",
43	    "             --runs times at --gap, collects each run's environment grade,\n",
44	    "             prints the table and a verdict: QUALIFIED when the median\n",
45	    "             grade is B or better and no run's drift or step reached D/F.\n",
46	    "             Exits nonzero when not. Grades the environment, not the run —\n",
47	    "             the machine is the subject, not a workload. Must stand alone;\n",
48	    "             -d sets each child's duration (default 1s), --pin passes\n",
49	    "             through, --print-only skips the verdict.\n",
50	    "  add-completion-yaml\n",
51	    "             install Tab completion (bench names, command words, flags)\n",
52	    "             for any carapace-served shell: generate the carapace spec\n",
53	    "             and write it to the specs dir as iiac-perf.yaml (see\n",
54	    "             --completion-dir), creating the dir and overwriting any\n",
55	    "             existing spec. Run once after install, again after an\n",

58	    "             alone.",

66	    ///
67	    /// Pass 'all' for every registered bench, or one or more

70	    /// 'qualify-environment' (alone) to ask whether this machine

80	    /// and inner loop counts. Mutually exclusive with -D.

82	    duration: Option<f64>,

85	    ///
86	    /// The budget is split equally per bench. Mutually exclusive
87	    /// with -d.

89	    total_duration: Option<f64>,
90	
91	    /// Override outer loop count (skips auto-sizing; inner still adapts).
92	    #[arg(short, long)]
93	    outer: Option<u64>,
94	
95	    /// Override inner loop count (skips auto-sizing).
96	    ///
97	    /// inner=1 measures single-call latency (each sample = one
98	    /// step); higher inner measures back-to-back/burst rate
99	    /// (each sample = N steps averaged).
100	    #[arg(short, long)]
101	    inner: Option<u64>,
102	
103	    /// Pin bench threads to logical CPUs (comma-separated, ranges OK).
104	    ///
105	    /// The list is a core *pool*: thread `i` of a bench is pinned to
106	    /// `pool[i % pool.len()]`, so shorter pools oversubscribe by wrap.
107	    /// Examples: `--pin 0,1` (2 threads → 2 CPUs), `--pin 0-5` (6-thread
108	    /// pool), `--pin 0,0` (two threads on the same CPU). On 3900X,
109	    /// logical CPUs N and N+12 are SMT siblings of the same physical
110	    /// core — `--pin 0,12` pairs siblings (max contention), `--pin 0,1`
111	    /// gives independent cores. A value naming a `[profiles]` entry in
112	    /// the config file expands to that profile's core spec (e.g.
113	    /// `--pin smt`). Omit to leave threads unpinned.
114	    #[arg(long, value_name = "CORES")]
115	    pin: Option<String>,
116	
117	    /// Enable verbose internals on stderr (like `RUST_LOG=debug`).
118	    ///
119	    /// Shows the affinity mask, the pin lifecycle, and the TSC
120	    /// tick rate. Default is `warn` (silent unless something's
121	    /// wrong). `RUST_LOG` overrides this flag when set, so
122	    /// per-module filtering still works.
123	    #[arg(short, long)]
124	    verbose: bool,
125	
126	    /// Show tprobe results in raw TSC ticks, not nanoseconds.
127	    ///
128	    /// Only affects `TProbe` output; `Probe` results are always
129	    /// in nanoseconds.
130	    #[arg(short = 't', long)]
131	    ticks: bool,
132	
133	    /// `qualify-environment` only: child runs to spawn.
134	    #[arg(long, value_name = "N", default_value_t = 10, value_parser = clap::value_parser!(u64).range(1..))]
135	    runs: u64,
136	
137	    /// `qualify-environment` only: seconds to sleep before each
138	    /// child run.
139	    ///
140	    /// Zero (the default) sustains the duty cycle that provokes a
141	    /// state transition; a nonzero gap probes a quieter one.
142	    #[arg(long, value_name = "SECONDS", default_value_t = 0.0)]
143	    gap: f64,
144	
145	    /// `qualify-environment` only: print the table and skip the
146	    /// verdict.
147	    #[arg(long)]
148	    print_only: bool,
149	
150	    /// Stop probing the environment at batch seams.
151	    ///
152	    /// The environment grade normally samples the box at every
153	    /// batch boundary, so its letter covers the whole run. This
154	    /// limits it to the warmup probes, which cover only the few
155	    /// ms before the bench starts. Use it when the seam probes
156	    /// disturb the workload — a spinning multi-threaded bench
157	    /// keeps running through a probe, so its queues drain — or
158	    /// to A/B whether they do.
159	    #[arg(long)]
160	    no_env_probe: bool,
161	
162	    /// Seconds to warm the box before the first bench measures.
163	    ///
164	    /// The first bench of a process otherwise reports a cold
165	    /// machine's numbers - measured at ~8.6% slow on a 7600x -
166	    /// while every later bench inherits the boosted state. The
167	    /// warm is paid once per process, not per bench, and the
168	    /// grade block's `settle` cell says how long the box actually
169	    /// took to settle. 0 skips it, which is how you measure what
170	    /// the warm is worth on a given box. Overrides the config
171	    /// `settle_time`; both absent defaults to 1.5.
172	    #[arg(long, value_name = "SECONDS", allow_negative_numbers = true)]
173	    settle_time: Option<f64>,
174	
175	    /// Cap on each run's warm-until-stable stretch (seconds).
176	    ///
177	    /// Every run warms until the trailing probe window grades A
178	    /// (and the delivered clock holds still, where readable), or
179	    /// until this cap. A settled box exits in ~50 ms; the cap
180	    /// prices only the disturbed case, and hitting it is
181	    /// reported in the grade block ("not settled" /
182	    /// "uncertified"), never silently absorbed. 0 caps
183	    /// immediately, which is how you measure what the warm is
184	    /// worth. Overrides the config `warm_cap`; both absent
185	    /// defaults to 1.5.
186	    #[arg(long, value_name = "SECONDS", allow_negative_numbers = true)]
187	    warm_cap: Option<f64>,
188	
189	    /// Band label style for the report's histogram rows.
190	    ///
191	    /// 'zpn': nines/zeros + decile names (z3, p50, n4).
192	    /// 'frac': literal boundary fractions with '_' grouping
193	    /// (0.001, 0.50, 0.999_9). 'both': zpn and fraction
194	    /// side by side — the juxtaposition teaches the zpn
195	    /// vocabulary; switch to 'zpn' once fluent. Overrides the
196	    /// config `band_labels`; both absent defaults to 'both'.
197	    #[arg(long, value_enum)]
198	    band_labels: Option<bands::BandLabels>,
199	
200	    /// Decimal digits on the report's time columns (0-3).
201	    ///
202	    /// 1 shows the sub-ns precision picosecond recording
203	    /// captures; 0 restores integer ns; 3 is the recording
204	    /// floor - more digits would be artifacts. Overrides the
205	    /// config `decimals`; both absent defaults to 1.
206	    #[arg(long, value_parser = clap::value_parser!(u8).range(0..=3))]
207	    decimals: Option<u8>,
208	
209	    /// Divide the run into N sleep-separated measurement blocks.
210	    ///
211	    /// E.g. `--blocks 10 -d 10` = 10 blocks of ~1 s each, with
212	    /// block-replication stats reported (mean blocks / CI95 /
213	    /// LSC). Each block sleeps a random 1-10 ms (re-rolls
214	    /// scheduler and frequency state) and warms up unrecorded
215	    /// before measuring; neither is counted in the budget. The
216	    /// spread of block means yields a per-run 95% confidence
217	    /// interval and least-significant-change estimate. Blocks
218	    /// nest above batches: each block is a contiguous stretch
219	    /// of whole batches (batch boundaries align to the block
220	    /// gaps), so batches stay the grade's time-series grain and
221	    /// blocks are the replication grain.
222	    /// Bench-driven benches only; probe benches ignore it.
223	    #[arg(long, value_name = "N", value_parser = clap::value_parser!(u64).range(2..=1000))]
224	    blocks: Option<u64>,
225	
226	    /// Do not inhibit system sleep for the run.
227	    ///
228	    /// By default the process re-execs itself under
229	    /// `systemd-inhibit --what=sleep` so an idle-suspend can't
230	    /// poison a long measurement. Pass this to keep the process
231	    /// image untouched (strace/gdb/perf wrappers), to let the
232	    /// machine sleep on purpose, or to test the suspend-detection
233	    /// WARNING path (a sleep inhibitor also blocks manual
234	    /// `systemctl suspend`).
235	    #[arg(long)]
236	    no_inhibit: bool,
237	
238	    /// Print a shell-completion artifact to stdout and exit.
239	    ///
240	    /// No bench runs: a static script for bash, zsh, fish,
241	    /// elvish, or powershell, or a spec for the carapace-bin
242	    /// multi-shell engine. Install e.g. `iiac-perf --completions
243	    /// bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/iiac-perf`;
244	    /// for carapace prefer the 'add-completion-yaml' command,
245	    /// which writes the spec to the specs dir itself.
246	    #[arg(long, value_enum, value_name = "SHELL")]
247	    completions: Option<CompletionShell>,
248	
249	    /// Directory for 'add-completion-yaml' to write iiac-perf.yaml.
250	    ///
251	    /// Defaults to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/carapace/specs, falling back
252	    /// to ~/.config/carapace/specs — carapace-bin's own spec
253	    /// lookup dir. The dir is created if missing and an existing
254	    /// spec is overwritten.
255	    #[arg(long, value_name = "DIR")]
256	    completion_dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
257	
258	    /// Print the registered bench names, one per line, and exit.
259	    ///
260	    /// No bench runs. Machine-readable: the carapace spec's
261	    /// exec-macro calls this at completion time for dynamic
262	    /// bench-name candidates (see --completions), and scripts can
263	    /// iterate it. The 'all' command word is not
264	    /// bench names and are not listed.
265	    #[arg(long, conflicts_with = "completions")]
266	    list_benches: bool,

292	/// Banner text listing which config files were loaded, or
293	/// `"none (built-in defaults)"` when neither file exists.

306	/// Print the `--completions` artifact for the chosen shell to
307	/// stdout: a clap_complete static script, or the carapace YAML
308	/// spec via the same `Generator` interface.
309	fn print_completions(shell: CompletionShell) {
310	    use clap_complete::{Shell, generate};
311	    let mut cmd = Cli::command();
312	    let out = &mut std::io::stdout();
313	    match shell {
314	        CompletionShell::Bash => generate(Shell::Bash, &mut cmd, "iiac-perf", out),
315	        CompletionShell::Zsh => generate(Shell::Zsh, &mut cmd, "iiac-perf", out),
316	        CompletionShell::Fish => generate(Shell::Fish, &mut cmd, "iiac-perf", out),
317	        CompletionShell::Elvish => generate(Shell::Elvish, &mut cmd, "iiac-perf", out),
318	        CompletionShell::Powershell => generate(Shell::PowerShell, &mut cmd, "iiac-perf", out),
319	        CompletionShell::Carapace => print!("{}", carapace_spec()),
320	    }

323	/// Render the carapace YAML spec (clap-generated plus the dynamic
324	/// bench-name injection) as a string — shared by `--completions
325	/// carapace` (stdout) and the 'add-completion-yaml' command (file).
326	fn carapace_spec() -> String {
327	    let mut cmd = Cli::command();
328	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
329	    clap_complete::generate(carapace_spec_clap::Spec, &mut cmd, "iiac-perf", &mut buf);
330	    inject_bench_candidates(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf))
331	}

333	/// Resolve the default carapace specs dir from the environment:
334	/// `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/carapace/specs`, falling back to
335	/// `$HOME/.config/carapace/specs` — mirroring carapace-bin's own
336	/// spec lookup. `None` when neither variable yields a base.
337	fn default_completion_dir() -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
338	    completion_dir_from(
339	        std::env::var_os("XDG_CONFIG_HOME"),
340	        std::env::var_os("HOME"),
341	    )
342	}
343	
344	/// Env-free core of [`default_completion_dir`], split out so unit
345	/// tests can drive it without mutating the process environment.
346	///
347	/// - a relative `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is ignored, per the XDG spec;
348	/// - an unset or empty `$HOME` yields `None` rather than a
349	///   relative `.config` path.
350	fn completion_dir_from(
351	    xdg: Option<std::ffi::OsString>,
352	    home: Option<std::ffi::OsString>,
353	) -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
354	    let base = match xdg.map(std::path::PathBuf::from) {
355	        Some(p) if p.is_absolute() => p,
356	        _ => {
357	            let home = home.filter(|h| !h.is_empty())?;
358	            std::path::PathBuf::from(home).join(".config")
359	        }
360	    };
361	    Some(base.join("carapace").join("specs"))
362	}
363	
364	/// Write the carapace spec to `dir/iiac-perf.yaml`, creating the
365	/// dir if needed and overwriting any existing spec; returns the
366	/// written path.
367	fn write_completion_yaml(dir: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
368	    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
369	    let path = dir.join("iiac-perf.yaml");
370	    std::fs::write(&path, carapace_spec())?;
371	    Ok(path)
372	}

374	/// Inject dynamic bench-name completion into the generated carapace
375	/// spec: a `positionalany` list whose exec-macro asks the installed
376	/// binary (`--list-benches`) on every Tab, plus the two static
377	/// command words. The generator emits only what clap knows, so the
378	/// positional would otherwise complete to nothing.
379	fn inject_bench_candidates(spec: &str) -> String {
380	    let block = concat!(
381	        "completion:\n",
382	        "  positionalany:\n",
383	        "  - \"$(iiac-perf --list-benches)\"\n",
384	        "  - \"all\\trun every registered bench\"\n",
385	        "  - \"qualify-environment\\tis this machine fit to measure on?\"\n",
386	        "  - \"add-completion-yaml\\twrite the carapace completion spec to the specs dir\"\n",
387	    );
388	    if spec.contains("completion:\n") {
389	        spec.replacen("completion:\n", block, 1)
390	    } else {
391	        format!("{spec}{block}")
392	    }
393	}
394	
395	/// Wrap a name list into comma-separated lines of at most `width`
396	/// columns, each line indented two spaces — the no-benches
397	/// listing's counterpart of clap's two-column help style.
398	fn wrap_names(names: &[&str], width: usize) -> String {
399	    let mut out = String::new();
400	    let mut col = 0;
401	    for name in names {
402	        if out.is_empty() {
403	            out.push_str("  ");
404	        } else if col + 2 + name.len() <= width {
405	            out.push_str(", ");
406	        } else {
407	            out.push_str(",\n  ");
408	            col = 0;
409	        }
410	        out.push_str(name);
411	        col += 2 + name.len();
412	    }
413	    out
414	}

416	fn main() {
417	    let cli = Cli::parse();
418	
419	    // Completion generation and the bench-name listing are pure
420	    // print-and-exit paths: no logging, no config, no setup.
421	    if let Some(shell) = cli.completions {
422	        print_completions(shell);
423	        return;
424	    }
425	    if cli.list_benches {
426	        for name in benches::names() {
427	            println!("{name}");
428	        }
429	        return;
430	    }
431	
432	    // 'add-completion-yaml' is a command word like 'all':
433	    // self-install the carapace spec, print the path, and exit.
434	    if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "add-completion-yaml") {
435	        if cli.benches.len() > 1 {
436	            eprintln!("error: 'add-completion-yaml' runs alone; drop the other bench args");
437	            std::process::exit(2);
438	        }
439	        let dir = match cli.completion_dir.clone().or_else(default_completion_dir) {
440	            Some(d) => d,
441	            None => {
442	                eprintln!(
443	                    "error: no specs dir ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME and $HOME unset); pass --completion-dir"
444	                );
445	                std::process::exit(2);
446	            }
447	        };
448	        match write_completion_yaml(&dir) {
449	            Ok(path) => println!("{}", path.display()),
450	            Err(e) => {
451	                eprintln!(
452	                    "error: writing {}: {e}",
453	                    dir.join("iiac-perf.yaml").display()
454	                );
455	                std::process::exit(1);
456	            }
457	        }
458	        return;
459	    }
460	
461	    // Default filter is `warn`; `-v` bumps to `debug`. `RUST_LOG`
462	    // (if set) always wins — so users can still do fine-grained
463	    // per-module filtering without fighting the flag.
464	    let mut builder = env_logger::Builder::from_default_env();
465	    if std::env::var_os("RUST_LOG").is_none() {
466	        builder.filter_level(if cli.verbose {
467	            log::LevelFilter::Debug
468	        } else {
469	            log::LevelFilter::Warn
470	        });
471	    }
472	    builder.format_timestamp(None).init();
473	
474	    if cli.benches.is_empty() {
475	        println!("{ABOUT}\n");
476	        println!("no benches specified. use -h or --help for more info.\n");
477	        println!("Benches:");
478	        println!("{}\n", wrap_names(&benches::names(), 72));
479	        println!("{COMMANDS_HELP}");
480	        // Nudge toward completion setup until the spec exists at
481	        // the default path; silent once installed (or if a custom
482	        // --completion-dir was used — only the default is checked).
483	        let spec_missing =
484	            default_completion_dir().is_some_and(|d| !d.join("iiac-perf.yaml").exists());
485	        if spec_missing {
486	            println!("\nFor command completion execute 'iiac-perf add-completion-yaml -h'");
487	        }
488	        return;
489	    }
490	
491	    // 'qualify-environment' is a command, not a bench: it respawns
492	    // --runs times and grades the box across those runs. It stands
493	    // alone, and it re-execs children itself, so it runs before
494	    // the inhibit/config/banner path a bench run needs.
495	    if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "qualify-environment") {
496	        if cli.benches.len() > 1 {
497	            eprintln!("error: 'qualify-environment' runs alone; drop the other bench args");
498	            std::process::exit(2);
499	        }
500	        println!("{ABOUT}\n");
501	        let code = qualify::run(&qualify::QualifyCfg {
502	            runs: cli.runs,
503	            gap_s: cli.gap,
504	            duration_s: cli.duration.unwrap_or(QUALIFY_CHILD_SECONDS),
505	            pin: cli.pin.clone(),
506	            print_only: cli.print_only,
507	            settle_time: cli.settle_time,
508	        });
509	        std::process::exit(code);
510	    }
511	
512	    // Re-exec under systemd-inhibit (unless --no-inhibit or
513	    // already inhibited) before any output, so the banner prints
514	    // once, from the inhibited child.
515	    let inhibit_status = inhibit::ensure(cli.no_inhibit);
516	
517	    // Layered defaults (built-in < XDG file < project-local file <
518	    // CLI). A malformed config is fatal so a typo surfaces.
519	    let (config, config_files) = match config::load() {
520	        Ok(c) => c,
521	        Err(e) => {
522	            eprintln!("error: config: {e}");
523	            std::process::exit(2);
524	        }
525	    };
526	
527	    println!("{ABOUT}\n");
528	
529	    if let Some(mask) = pin::current_affinity() {
530	        info!("startup affinity: {}", pin::affinity_summary(&mask));
531	    }
532	
533	    let pin_cores: Vec<usize> = match cli.pin.as_deref() {
534	        None => Vec::new(),
535	        // A spec naming a config profile expands to its core list;
536	        // anything else parses as a raw core spec.
537	        Some(spec) => match pin::parse_cores(config.resolve_pin(spec)) {
538	            Ok(v) => v,
539	            Err(e) => {
540	                eprintln!("error: --pin: {e}");
541	                std::process::exit(2);
542	            }
543	        },
544	    };
545	
546	    // Pin main to the pool's first slot when --pin is given: thread 0 of a bench measures on
547	    // main, and the warm loop is a real timing phase converging on per-core frequency state, so
548	    // it must run where measurement will run. Without --pin, main stays wherever the scheduler
549	    // has it: a busy thread stays put, and the warm state lands on the core that measures. The
550	    // retired CPU0-default warm pin parked the warm on the kernel's busiest core for no
551	    // measured benefit: the tick-rate read is a ratio that cancels interruptions (~8e-7 spread
552	    // across cores), and nothing else ran pinned.
553	    if let Some(&cpu) = pin_cores.first() {
554	        pin::pin_current(Some(cpu));
555	        info!("pinned main to core {cpu} (bench pin pool slot 0)");
556	    }
557	    if let Some(mask) = pin::current_affinity() {
558	        debug!("affinity for warm + run: {}", pin::affinity_summary(&mask));
559	    }
560	
561	    // Warm the one-time TSC tick-rate calibration (a ~10 ms spin behind a OnceLock) here on
562	    // main. Without this the first TProbe::new in a bench thread pays it inside the measurement
563	    // window: a short -d (e.g. 0.01) was consumed entirely by that spin and recorded zero
564	    // samples.
565	    let ticks_per_ns = ticks::ticks_per_ns();
566	    debug!("ticks_per_ns: {ticks_per_ns:.6}");
567	
568	    // Same precedence as duration: CLI, then config, then the
569	    // built-in. Negative is rejected rather than clamped: it
570	    // means the caller expected something we don't do.
571	    let settle_time = cli
572	        .settle_time
573	        .or(config.settle_time)
574	        .unwrap_or(harness::DEFAULT_SETTLE_TIME_S);
575	    if settle_time < 0.0 {
576	        eprintln!("error: --settle-time must be zero or more, got {settle_time}");
577	        std::process::exit(2);
578	    }
579	
580	    // Same precedence as settle time: CLI, then config, then the built-in.
581	    let warm_cap = cli
582	        .warm_cap
583	        .or(config.warm_cap)
584	        .unwrap_or(harness::DEFAULT_WARM_CAP_S);
585	    if warm_cap < 0.0 {
586	        eprintln!("error: --warm-cap must be zero or more, got {warm_cap}");
587	        std::process::exit(2);
588	    }
589	
590	    // Main's placement covers the warm loop and thread 0 of every bench, so the cell names
591	    // both.
592	    let main_pin_display = match pin_cores.first() {
593	        Some(c) => format!("core {c} (pool slot 0; warm + run)"),
594	        None => "none (scheduler placement)".to_string(),
595	    };
596	    // The box's clock and power policy, printed before any bench so every archived report says
597	    // what machine produced it. No report before 0.25.0 recorded the policy, which left an 8.9%
598	    // governor delta indistinguishable from a code change in any A/B spanning one.
599	    let policy = freq::policy();
600	    let boost = policy.boost.as_ref().map(|f| freq::PolicyField {
601	        value: boost_word(&f.value).to_string(),
602	        uniform: f.uniform,
603	    });
604	    println!("Setup:");
605	    println!("  ticks/ns          {ticks_per_ns:.6}");
606	    println!("  tick period       {:.3} ns", 1.0 / ticks_per_ns);
607	    println!(
608	        "  cpufreq driver    {}",
609	        policy_cell(policy.driver.as_ref())
610	    );
611	    println!(
612	        "  governor          {}",
613	        policy_cell(policy.governor.as_ref())
614	    );
615	    println!("  EPP               {}", policy_cell(policy.epp.as_ref()));
616	    println!("  boost             {}", policy_cell(boost.as_ref()));
617	    println!("  main pin          {main_pin_display}");
618	    println!("  bench pin         {}", pin::plan_summary(&pin_cores));
619	    // The budgets, not the spend: each run's report brackets carry
620	    // its own warm=used/cap, and the grade block's settle cell says
621	    // when the box settled.
622	    println!("  warm budget       settle {settle_time}s once + cap {warm_cap}s per run");
623	    println!("  sleep inhibit     {inhibit_status}");
624	    println!("  config            {}", config_summary(&config_files));
625	    println!();
626	
627	    let runners = match benches::resolve(&cli.benches) {
628	        Ok(r) => r,
629	        Err(e) => {
630	            eprintln!("error: {e}");
631	            std::process::exit(2);
632	        }
633	    };
634	
635	    // Duration precedence: CLI -d / -D win, then the config
636	    // `duration`, then the built-in default.
637	    let target_seconds = match (cli.duration, cli.total_duration) {
638	        (Some(d), _) => d,
639	        (None, Some(t)) => t / runners.len() as f64,
640	        (None, None) => config.duration.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_DURATION),
641	    };
642	
643	    let cfg = harness::RunCfg {
644	        target_seconds,
645	        outer_override: cli.outer,
646	        inner_override: cli.inner,
647	        pin_cores: &pin_cores,
648	        report_ticks: cli.ticks,
649	        seam_probes: !cli.no_env_probe,
650	        band_labels: cli
651	            .band_labels
652	            .or(config.band_labels)
653	            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_BAND_LABELS),
654	        decimals: cli.decimals.or(config.decimals).unwrap_or(DEFAULT_DECIMALS) as usize,
655	        settle_time_s: settle_time,
656	        warm_cap_s: warm_cap,
657	        blocks: cli.blocks,
658	    };
659	
660	    for run in runners {
661	        run(&cfg);
662	    }
663	}
664	
665	/// Render one `Setup:` policy cell: the token, marked when CPUs disagree, or why it is absent.
666	///
667	/// - `None` prints `not exposed` and never a default. A box without the file has no such
668	///   policy, and inventing one is exactly what makes an archived number ambiguous.
669	/// - A non-uniform field carries `(mixed across CPUs)`: one CPU's token is not the box's policy
670	///   when the policy groups were set separately.
671	fn policy_cell(field: Option<&freq::PolicyField>) -> String {
672	    match field {
673	        None => "not exposed".to_string(),
674	        Some(f) if f.uniform => f.value.clone(),
675	        Some(f) => format!("{} (mixed across CPUs)", f.value),
676	    }
677	}
678	
679	/// `boost`'s raw sysfs token as a word; anything unrecognized passes through untranslated
680	/// rather than being guessed at.
681	fn boost_word(raw: &str) -> &str {
682	    match raw {
683	        "1" => "enabled",
684	        "0" => "disabled",
685	        other => other,
686	    }
687	}
688	
689	#[cfg(test)]
690	mod tests {
691	    use super::*;
692	
693	    fn policy_field(value: &str, uniform: bool) -> freq::PolicyField {
694	        freq::PolicyField {
695	            value: value.to_string(),
696	            uniform,
697	        }
698	    }
699	
700	    #[test]
701	    fn policy_cell_says_absent_rather_than_defaulting() {
702	        assert_eq!(policy_cell(None), "not exposed");
703	    }
704	
705	    #[test]
706	    fn policy_cell_marks_a_split_policy() {
707	        assert_eq!(
708	            policy_cell(Some(&policy_field("powersave", true))),
709	            "powersave"
710	        );
711	        assert_eq!(
712	            policy_cell(Some(&policy_field("powersave", false))),
713	            "powersave (mixed across CPUs)"
714	        );
715	    }
716	
717	    #[test]
718	    fn boost_word_translates_only_the_known_tokens() {
719	        assert_eq!(boost_word("1"), "enabled");
720	        assert_eq!(boost_word("0"), "disabled");
721	        assert_eq!(boost_word("unexpected"), "unexpected");
722	    }
723	
724	    #[test]
725	    fn wrap_names_single_line() {
726	        assert_eq!(wrap_names(&["a", "b"], 72), "  a, b");
727	    }
728	
729	    #[test]
730	    fn inject_bench_candidates_precedes_flag_section() {
731	        let spec = "name: x\ncompletion:\n  flag:\n    a:\n    - one\n";
732	        let out = inject_bench_candidates(spec);
733	        // positionalany lands under the existing completion key,
734	        // before the flag section; the exec-macro is quoted.
735	        let pos = out.find("  positionalany:").expect("positionalany missing");
736	        let flag = out.find("  flag:").expect("flag section missing");
737	        assert!(pos < flag);
738	        assert!(out.contains("\"$(iiac-perf --list-benches)\""));
739	        assert_eq!(out.matches("completion:\n").count(), 1);
740	    }
741	
742	    #[test]
743	    fn inject_bench_candidates_appends_when_no_completion_key() {
744	        let out = inject_bench_candidates("name: x\n");
745	        assert!(out.ends_with(
746	            "- \"add-completion-yaml\\twrite the carapace completion spec to the specs dir\"\n"
747	        ));
748	        assert!(out.contains("completion:\n  positionalany:\n"));
749	    }
750	
751	    #[test]
752	    fn completion_dir_prefers_absolute_xdg() {
753	        let dir = completion_dir_from(Some("/xdg".into()), Some("/home/u".into()));
754	        assert_eq!(dir, Some("/xdg/carapace/specs".into()));
755	    }
756	
757	    #[test]
758	    fn completion_dir_ignores_relative_xdg() {
759	        let dir = completion_dir_from(Some("rel".into()), Some("/home/u".into()));
760	        assert_eq!(dir, Some("/home/u/.config/carapace/specs".into()));
761	    }
762	
763	    #[test]
764	    fn completion_dir_none_without_home() {
765	        assert_eq!(completion_dir_from(None, None), None);
766	        assert_eq!(completion_dir_from(None, Some("".into())), None);
767	    }
768	
769	    #[test]
770	    fn wrap_names_breaks_at_width() {
771	        // "ccc" would land past col 10, so it wraps; the separator
772	        // comma stays on the prior line and the new line re-indents.
773	        assert_eq!(wrap_names(&["aaa", "bbb", "ccc"], 10), "  aaa, bbb,\n  ccc");

1	//! Generic bench driver: the [`Bench`] trait, the warm loop, adaptive outer/inner loop sizing,
2	//! and the batch/block pipeline that turns a workload into a [`RunOutput`].
3	//!
4	//! Measuring only. Rendering that `RunOutput` into text is [`crate::report`], which this module
5	//! never calls: the value is the seam, and it flows one way.
6	
7	use std::hint::black_box;
8	
9	use hdrhistogram::Histogram;
10	
11	use crate::bands::BandLabels;
12	use crate::dither::Dither;
13	
14	const FRAMING_DOMINATION_RATIO: f64 = 10.0;
15	const MAX_INNER: u64 = 1_000;
16	
17	/// Minimum bench steps in one warmup pass, so a pass's per-step
18	/// cost (the sizing input) is never one sample.
19	///
20	/// - Small on purpose: for cheap steps the wall minimum ([`WARM_PASS_MIN_SECONDS`]) dominates
21	///   anyway, and a large count would hold a genuinely slow bench (ms-scale steps) far past the
22	///   cap before its first pass ended.
23	const WARM_PASS_MIN_STEPS: u64 = 8;
24	
25	/// Minimum wall seconds in one warmup pass: with [`WARM_PASS_MIN_STEPS`], "whichever is larger"
26	/// sets the pass length, so a pass is a real burst of load rather than a blink.
27	const WARM_PASS_MIN_SECONDS: f64 = 0.001;
28	
29	/// Ceiling on the step chunk between elapsed checks inside an adaptive warmup pass. The chunk
30	/// starts at 1 and doubles, so a cheap bench amortizes `Instant::now` out of its measured pass
31	/// cost while a slow bench still gets a deadline check every step (the estimate-phase hang this
32	/// replaces, bugs.md #1).
33	const WARM_STEP_CHUNK_MAX: u64 = 64;
34	
35	/// Minimum probes in the warm exit window: the split detector wants 4 points a side.
36	const WARM_WINDOW_MIN_PROBES: usize = 8;
37	
38	/// Minimum wall span of the warm exit window (seconds).
39	///
40	/// - A window can be far shorter than what it certifies: 16 probes of the retired fixed warmup
41	///   spanned ~17 us against a transition arriving at ~800 ms, so agreement alone certifies
42	///   nothing. The span makes the window a statement about held time.
43	/// - 50 ms is governor-transition scale (single P-state moves land in tens of ms), not
44	///   full-ramp scale: the exit rule already guarantees the window sits after any movement it
45	///   can see, so unlike the retired fixed 300 ms tail it does not need to be long enough to
46	///   *contain* a ramp. What a timing window cannot see at any length (a steady dwell below the
47	///   top) is the clock rung's job.
48	const WARM_WINDOW_MIN_SECONDS: f64 = 0.05;
49	
50	/// Default hard cap on the per-run warm stretch (seconds): the `--warm-cap` / `warm_cap`
51	/// default ([`RunCfg::warm_cap_s`]). Hitting the cap is reported, never silently absorbed: the
52	/// window's actual grade stands (the "run started unstable" signal), or the run is labelled
53	/// uncertified when no window ever formed ([`WarmExit`]). The cap also deadlines every
54	/// adaptive pass, so a pathologically slow bench exits with a diagnosis instead of hanging in
55	/// an open step loop.
56	///
57	/// - 1.5 s rather than governor scale (the 0.4 s it started at): the 3900X's relaxation
58	///   re-ramp measured ~0.7 to 1.4 s on 2026-08-02's acceptance runs, and a cap below it turns
59	///   an absorbable ramp into a "not settled" report. A settled box exits in ~50 ms regardless;
60	///   the cap prices only the disturbed case.
61	pub const DEFAULT_WARM_CAP_S: f64 = 1.5;
62	
63	/// Timer pairs per *timed group* inside a micro-probe.
64	///
65	/// - The probe's unit of measurement is a group, not a single
66	///   pair: one `Instant` pair brackets [`PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS`]
67	///   pairs and the total is divided down to a per-pair value.
68	/// - **Why group at all:** the timer reads integer nanoseconds,
69	///   so a single ~25 ns pair is quantized to ~4% — coarser than
70	///   the frequency-ramp movement the environment grade exists to
71	///   see (~9% on the 3900X). A 64-pair group totals ~1.6 µs, so
72	///   the same 1 ns quantum is ~0.06% of the value, and the
73	///   per-pair figure lands on a ~15 ps lattice.
74	/// - Grouping costs the *census* its sensitivity, so the census
75	///   is counted per pair instead — see [`Prober::probe`].
76	const PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS: usize = 64;
77	
78	/// Timed groups per micro-probe — the population its floor and
79	/// spread quantiles are taken over.
80	///
81	/// - 128 groups of [`PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS`] is ~8,192 pairs, about
82	///   256 µs. Sized against the batch seam it runs in, which
83	///   already costs 1-2 ms (a `select_nth_unstable` plus 65,536
84	///   histogram records), so a probe adds a fraction of a gap
85	///   that already exists rather than a new one.
86	const PROBE_GROUPS: usize = 128;
87	
88	/// Initial capacity of the warmup probe series: a settled box exits with
89	/// ~[`WARM_WINDOW_MIN_SECONDS`] of ~1 ms passes, so ~64 probes; a first run's process warm adds
90	/// ~150.
91	const WARM_PROBES_CAPACITY: usize = 64;
92	
93	/// Default wall seconds the **first** run in a process spends
94	/// stepping the bench before any samples are recorded: the
95	/// `--settle-time` / `settle_time` default.
96	///
97	/// - **The first bench of every process reports numbers ~8.6%
98	///   slow otherwise.** Measured on a 7600x 2026-07-29: `min-now`
99	///   reads 17.6 ns as the process's first bench against 16.2 ns
100	///   once warm, and its env bench stretch grades `step 11.05% F`
101	///   while benches
102	///   2-17 of the same process grade env-clean. The P-state boost
103	///   is machine state, so every later bench inherits it. The
104	///   warm belongs to the process, not to each run.
105	/// - 1.5 s rather than 1.0: the ramp measured at ~150-200 ms but
106	///   the 3900X's relaxation lands later, and the exit window
107	///   ([`WARM_WINDOW_MIN_SECONDS`]) needs settled time behind it.
108	/// - Cost is ~2% of an `all -d 5` sweep (~85 s to ~86.5 s), paid
109	///   once, against a wrong histogram on whichever bench ran
110	///   first.
111	pub const DEFAULT_SETTLE_TIME_S: f64 = 1.5;
112	
113	/// Wall seconds of stepping between micro-probes during the
114	/// process warm: ~150 probes over [`DEFAULT_SETTLE_TIME_S`], so
115	/// the series resolves a transition to ~10 ms and the exit
116	/// window holds several probes even before any per-run pass.
117	const PROCESS_WARM_PROBE_GAP_S: f64 = 0.01;
118	
119	/// Steps between elapsed-time checks during the process warm, so
120	/// a cheap bench doesn't spend the warm inside `Instant::now`.
121	const PROCESS_WARM_STEP_CHUNK: usize = 64;
122	
123	/// Quantile defining a micro-probe's floor, matching
124	/// [`BATCH_FLOOR_Q`]'s reasoning: the left edge is sparse, a
125	/// tenth of the population is not.
126	const ENV_FLOOR_Q: f64 = 0.10;
127	
128	/// Upper quantile paired with [`ENV_FLOOR_Q`] to measure a
129	/// probe's spread — how wide the bulk of the distribution sits
130	/// above its own floor.
131	const ENV_SPREAD_Q: f64 = 0.90;
132	
133	/// Census threshold for a micro-probe group, the batch census
134	/// rule ([`BATCH_OVER_MULT`]) rebased on the probe's scale: the
135	/// additive term is 5 ns rather than 50, because a per-pair
136	/// value is ~25 ns and a 50 ns floor would never be crossed.
137	const ENV_OVER_ADD_PS: u64 = 5_000;
138	
139	/// Batch buffer capacity in samples — the pipeline's memory
140	/// bound (512 KiB of u64 ps values). Fast benches fill it in
141	/// ~15–40 ms and flush full; slow benches flush earlier on
142	/// [`BATCH_TARGET_SECONDS`].
143	pub(crate) const BATCH_SAMPLES: usize = 65_536;
144	
145	/// Time-based batch flush (seconds): a partial batch flushes
146	/// once it spans this long, so slow benches still get a usable
147	/// time axis (drift/burst localization) from few samples.
148	pub(crate) const BATCH_TARGET_SECONDS: f64 = 0.05;
149	
150	/// Push-count mask between time checks in
151	/// [`BatchPipeline::push`] — one `Instant::now` per 1024
152	/// samples keeps the check cost off the per-sample path.
153	const BATCH_CHECK_MASK: usize = 1023;
154	
155	/// Quantile defining a batch's *robust* floor, the statistic the
156	/// gauge's drift/step signals read.
157	///
158	/// - The raw min is too sparse to grade movement: measured on a
159	///   quiet 3900X at inner=10 (100 ps lattice), adjacent batch
160	///   minima flipped between 22.0 and 23.0 ns — a 4.5% "step" on
161	///   a run with no state change, which alone would have graded
162	///   every quiet run F.
163	/// - The same batches' p10 sat on 23.0 ns run-wide and moved
164	///   only when the machine did. The left edge of the
165	///   distribution is sparse; a tenth of 65,536 samples is not.
166	pub(crate) const BATCH_FLOOR_Q: f64 = 0.10;
167	
168	/// Census threshold: a batch sample is "over floor" above
169	/// `max(BATCH_OVER_MULT x floor, floor + BATCH_OVER_ADD_PS)`,
170	/// applied per batch against the batch's own [`BATCH_FLOOR_Q`]
171	/// floor.
172	///
173	/// - Measured against the raw min instead, the census was
174	///   meaningless on any bench with a low tail: mpsc-2t batches
175	///   whose min landed on a 0.9 µs fast path (against a 6.5 µs
176	///   floor) counted 99.9% of their samples "over floor", and the
177	///   ones whose min landed normally counted 1%.
178	const BATCH_OVER_MULT: f64 = 1.5;
179	
180	/// Additive part of the census threshold (50 ns in ps).
181	const BATCH_OVER_ADD_PS: u64 = 50_000;
182	
183	/// Sleep-separated blocks: random sleep bounds (ms) between
184	/// blocks. Randomized so block boundaries don't phase-lock with
185	/// kernel ticks or workload periodicity; long enough to let the
186	/// scheduler / frequency state re-roll.
187	const BLOCK_SLEEP_MS_MIN: u64 = 1;
188	const BLOCK_SLEEP_MS_MAX: u64 = 10;
189	
190	/// Unrecorded post-wake warm-up per block (seconds). Each wake
191	/// pays a frequency ramp plus a cache refill, which must not leak
192	/// into the block's samples.
193	const BLOCK_WARMUP_SECONDS: f64 = 0.002;
194	
195	/// Histogram value bounds: 1 ps to 60 s at 3 sig figs. Values
196	/// are recorded in **picoseconds** — the timer reads integer ns,
197	/// but dividing a sample by `inner` in ps keeps the true sub-ns
198	/// per-call precision that ns recording truncated (a 4.7 ns call
199	/// no longer rounds to 5). The high bound is a sane-world
200	/// ceiling for one recorded sample, not a technical limit —
201	/// [`record_sample`] clamps above it and [`crate::report::warn_invalid`] flags
202	/// the run.
203	const HIST_LOW_PS: u64 = 1;
204	pub const HIST_HIGH_PS: u64 = 60_000_000_000_000;
205	
206	/// Picoseconds per nanosecond: recorded values are ps, display
207	/// is ns.
208	pub const PS_PER_NS: f64 = 1000.0;
209	
210	/// A benchmark workload: a named operation that `step()` performs
211	/// in a tight loop for sub-µs latency measurement. Implementors own
212	/// any setup state (channels, spawned threads, counters). `step()`
213	/// returns a value so the caller can `black_box` it against dead-code
214	/// elimination.
215	pub trait Bench {
216	    /// Human-readable name used in the report header.
217	    fn name(&self) -> &str;
218	
219	    /// Run one unit of work. Return any value derived from the work
220	    /// to defeat DCE — the caller black-boxes it.
221	    fn step(&mut self) -> u64;
222	}
223	
224	/// Runtime configuration for one [`run_adaptive`] call.
225	#[derive(Debug)]
226	pub struct RunCfg<'a> {
227	    /// Wall-clock seconds budget for time-based runs. Ignored when
228	    /// `outer_override` is set.
229	    pub target_seconds: f64,
230	    /// Force a fixed outer-loop count, bypassing the time budget.
231	    pub outer_override: Option<u64>,
232	    /// Force a fixed inner-loop count, bypassing the
233	    /// micro-probe-driven auto-sizing.
234	    pub inner_override: Option<u64>,
235	    /// Core pool for thread pinning. Indexed positionally with
236	    /// wrap-around via [`core_for`][RunCfg::core_for]; empty means
237	    /// no pinning.
238	    pub pin_cores: &'a [usize],
239	    /// When set, [`crate::tprobe::TProbe::report`] emits raw TSC
240	    /// ticks instead of nanoseconds. Plumbed from the `-t/--ticks`
241	    /// CLI flag.
242	    pub report_ticks: bool,
243	    /// Sample the environment at every batch seam, so the
244	    /// environment grade spans the whole run. Cleared by
245	    /// `--no-env-probe`, which leaves only the warmup probes.
246	    /// Plumbed from the CLI.
247	    pub seam_probes: bool,
248	    /// Band-label style for [`crate::report::print_report`] histogram rows.
249	    /// Plumbed from the `--band-labels` CLI flag.
250	    pub band_labels: BandLabels,
251	    /// Decimal digits on [`crate::report::print_report`] time columns. Plumbed
252	    /// from the `--decimals` CLI flag (default 1; 0 restores
253	    /// integers; 3 is the ps recording floor).
254	    pub decimals: usize,
255	    /// Seconds the first run in the process spends warming the
256	    /// box before it records anything; zero skips the warm. Later
257	    /// runs in the same process inherit the machine state it won,
258	    /// so the cost is paid once. Plumbed from `--settle-time` /
259	    /// the `settle_time` config key, defaulting to
260	    /// [`DEFAULT_SETTLE_TIME_S`].
261	    pub settle_time_s: f64,
262	    /// Hard cap on the per-run warm-until-stable stretch (seconds); hitting it is reported
263	    /// ([`WarmExit`]), never silently absorbed. Plumbed from `--warm-cap` / the `warm_cap`
264	    /// config key, defaulting to [`DEFAULT_WARM_CAP_S`]. Zero caps immediately, which is how a
265	    /// run measures what the warm is worth.
266	    pub warm_cap_s: f64,
267	    /// Split the run into this many sleep-separated blocks and
268	    /// report block-replication stats (mean ± 95% CI, LSC).
269	    /// Plumbed from the `--blocks` CLI flag; `None` = single
270	    /// continuous run. See
271	    /// notes/design.md#within-invocation-replication-sleep-separated-blocks.
272	    pub blocks: Option<u64>,
273	}
274	
275	impl RunCfg<'_> {
276	    /// CPU id for the bench's `thread_idx`-th thread, using
277	    /// wrap-around over the pool. Returns `None` when the pool is
278	    /// empty so callers can treat unpinned and pinned runs uniformly.
279	    pub fn core_for(&self, thread_idx: usize) -> Option<usize> {
280	        if self.pin_cores.is_empty() {
281	            None
282	        } else {
283	            Some(self.pin_cores[thread_idx % self.pin_cores.len()])
284	        }
285	    }
286	}
287	
288	/// Block-replication statistics from a sleep-separated run —
289	/// each block is a mini-run (own sleep re-roll + warm-up), so the
290	/// spread of block means yields an honest-per-invocation CI and
291	/// LSC. See
292	/// notes/design.md#within-invocation-replication-sleep-separated-blocks.
293	#[derive(Debug)]
294	pub struct BlockStats {
295	    /// Number of blocks (Y).
296	    pub blocks: u64,
297	    /// Mean of the per-block means, ns.
298	    pub mean_ns: f64,
299	    /// 95% confidence half-width on `mean_ns`:
300	    /// `t(0.975, Y-1) * s / sqrt(Y)`, ns.
301	    pub ci95_ns: f64,
302	    /// Least significant change vs an equal-Y run of another
303	    /// implementation: `t(0.975, 2Y-2) * s * sqrt(2/Y)`, ns.
304	    pub lsc_ns: f64,
305	}
306	
307	impl BlockStats {
308	    /// Fit from per-block means (ns). Caller guarantees
309	    /// `means.len() >= 2` (the CLI enforces `--blocks 2..`).
310	    fn from_means(means: &[f64]) -> BlockStats {
311	        let y = means.len() as f64;
312	        let mean = means.iter().sum::<f64>() / y;
313	        let var = means.iter().map(|m| (m - mean) * (m - mean)).sum::<f64>() / (y - 1.0);
314	        let s = var.sqrt();
315	        let yy = means.len() as u64;
316	        BlockStats {
317	            blocks: yy,
318	            mean_ns: mean,
319	            ci95_ns: t975(yy - 1) * s / y.sqrt(),
320	            lsc_ns: t975(2 * yy - 2) * s * (2.0 / y).sqrt(),
321	        }
322	    }
323	}
324	
325	/// Two-sided 95% Student-t quantile (`t(0.975, df)`), table for
326	/// df ≤ 30, then the conservative 2.0 (the true value falls from
327	/// 2.042 toward the normal 1.96).
328	fn t975(df: u64) -> f64 {
329	    const TABLE: [f64; 30] = [
330	        12.706, 4.303, 3.182, 2.776, 2.571, 2.447, 2.365, 2.306, 2.262, 2.228, 2.201, 2.179, 2.160,
331	        2.145, 2.131, 2.120, 2.110, 2.101, 2.093, 2.086, 2.080, 2.074, 2.069, 2.064, 2.060, 2.056,
332	        2.052, 2.048, 2.045, 2.042,
333	    ];
334	    match df {
335	        0 => f64::INFINITY,
336	        1..=30 => TABLE[(df - 1) as usize],
337	        _ => 2.0,
338	    }
339	}
340	
341	/// Everything a finished [`run_adaptive`] run produced — the
342	/// histogram plus the metadata [`crate::report::print_report`] needs and the
343	/// time-ordered [`BatchSummary`] series the gauge reads.
344	#[derive(Debug)]
345	pub struct RunOutput {
346	    /// Per-call values (ps) of every sample.
347	    pub hist: Histogram<u64>,
348	    /// Samples taken (outer-loop count).
349	    pub outer: u64,
350	    /// Calls per sample (inner-loop count).

395	/// Drive `bench` against `cfg` and return a [`RunOutput`].
396	///
397	/// After warming until stable (see [`warmup_and_probe`]), `inner` is auto-sized so apparatus
398	/// framing doesn't dominate (skipped when `cfg.inner_override` is set). The outer loop runs
399	/// either for `cfg.outer_override` iterations or until `cfg.target_seconds` elapses, as one
400	/// continuous run or split into `cfg.blocks` sleep-separated blocks (`block_stats` is `Some`
401	/// only then). Samples flow through the [`BatchPipeline`], so the output carries the run's time
402	/// axis as per-batch summaries alongside the histogram.
403	pub fn run_adaptive<B: Bench>(bench: &mut B, cfg: &RunCfg) -> RunOutput {
404	    let warmed = warmup_and_probe(bench, cfg.settle_time_s, cfg.warm_cap_s);
405	
406	    // The last warmup probe is the most-warmed one, so sizing reads a post-warmup
407	    // frame by construction; the step cost is the exit window's best pass
408	    // ([`Warmed::step_cost_ns`]).
409	    let frame_ns = match warmed.probes.last() {
410	        Some(p) => (p.floor_q_ps as f64 / PS_PER_NS).max(1.0),
411	        None => 1.0,
412	    };
413	    let inner = cfg
414	        .inner_override
415	        .unwrap_or_else(|| pick_inner(warmed.step_cost_ns, frame_ns));
416	
417	    let Warmed {
418	        origin,
419	        probes: warm_probes,
420	        prober,
421	        exit: warm_exit,
422	        tail: warm_tail,
423	        clock: warm_clock,
424	        settle: warm_settle,
425	        used_s: warm_used_s,
426	        budget_s: warm_budget_s,
427	        ..
428	    } = warmed;
429	    let warmup_probes = warm_probes.len();
430	    let mut pipeline = BatchPipeline::new(origin, prober, warm_probes, cfg.seam_probes);
431	    let clocks = ClockPair::now();
432	    let (block_stats, duration_s) = match cfg.blocks {
433	        Some(blocks) => {
434	            let (duration_s, stats) = run_blocked(
435	                bench,
436	                &mut pipeline,
437	                blocks,
438	                cfg.outer_override,
439	                cfg.target_seconds,
440	                inner,
441	            );
442	            (Some(stats), duration_s)
443	        }
444	        None => match cfg.outer_override {
445	            Some(outer) => (None, run_counted(bench, &mut pipeline, outer, inner)),
446	            None => (
447	                None,
448	                run_timed(bench, &mut pipeline, cfg.target_seconds, inner),
449	            ),
450	        },
451	    };
452	    let (hist, batches, probes) = pipeline.finish();
453	    let outer = match cfg.outer_override {
454	        Some(outer) if cfg.blocks.is_none() => outer,
455	        _ => hist.len(),
456	    };
457	    RunOutput {
458	        hist,
459	        outer,
460	        inner,
461	        duration_s,
462	        suspended_s: clocks.suspended_s(),
463	        block_stats,
464	        batches,
465	        probes,
466	        warmup_probes,
467	        warm_exit,
468	        warm_tail,
469	        warm_clock,
470	        warm_settle,
471	        warm_used_s,
472	        warm_budget_s,
473	    }
474	}

476	/// Run `blocks` sleep-separated blocks: each block sleeps a
477	/// random [`BLOCK_SLEEP_MS_MIN`]..=[`BLOCK_SLEEP_MS_MAX`] ms
478	/// (re-rolls scheduler / frequency / mode-mix state), steps
479	/// unrecorded for [`BLOCK_WARMUP_SECONDS`] (post-wake ramp), then
480	/// measures its share of the budget (`outer / blocks` samples, or
481	/// `target_seconds / blocks`). All samples land in one histogram;
482	/// per-block means feed [`BlockStats`]. The returned duration is
483	/// wall time including sleeps and warm-ups.
484	fn run_blocked<B: Bench>(
485	    bench: &mut B,
486	    pipeline: &mut BatchPipeline,
487	    blocks: u64,
488	    outer_override: Option<u64>,
489	    target_seconds: f64,
490	    inner: u64,
491	) -> (f64, BlockStats) {
492	    let mut dither = Dither::new();
493	    let mut means: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks as usize);
494	    let run_start = std::time::Instant::now();
495	    for b in 0..blocks {
496	        let ms =
497	            BLOCK_SLEEP_MS_MIN + dither.rand_u64() % (BLOCK_SLEEP_MS_MAX - BLOCK_SLEEP_MS_MIN + 1);
498	        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(ms));
499	
500	        warm_loop(
501	            bench,
502	            WarmPass::Seconds {
503	                s: BLOCK_WARMUP_SECONDS,
504	                chunk: 1,
505	            },
506	            None,
507	            |_, n| n >= 1,
508	        );
509	        // Align batch boundaries to blocks: the flush moves the
510	        // batch clock past the sleep + warmup gap, so no batch
511	        // spans time the bench wasn't running.
512	        pipeline.flush();
513	
514	        let mut sum_ps: u128 = 0;
515	        let mut n: u64 = 0;
516	        match outer_override {
517	            Some(outer) => {
518	                // Distribute the remainder over the first blocks.
519	                let count = outer / blocks + u64::from(b < outer % blocks);
520	                for _ in 0..count {
521	                    sum_ps += u128::from(record_sample(bench, inner, pipeline, &mut dither));
522	                    n += 1;
523	                }
524	            }
525	            None => {
526	                let budget = target_seconds / blocks as f64;
527	                let block_start = std::time::Instant::now();
528	                loop {
529	                    sum_ps += u128::from(record_sample(bench, inner, pipeline, &mut dither));
530	                    n += 1;
531	                    if block_start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() >= budget {
532	                        break;
533	                    }
534	                }
535	            }
536	        }
537	        pipeline.flush();
538	        if n > 0 {
539	            means.push(sum_ps as f64 / n as f64 / PS_PER_NS);
540	        }
541	    }
542	    let duration_s = run_start.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / 1e9;
543	    let stats = BlockStats::from_means(&means);
544	    (duration_s, stats)
545	}

547	/// Summary of one micro-probe — the environment's time axis, the
548	/// warmup-side counterpart to [`BatchSummary`].
549	///
550	/// - The probe measures the apparatus alone (timer pairs), never
551	///   the bench, so every field describes the *box* rather than
552	///   the workload. That is what makes it gradeable as an
553	///   environment certificate: see [`crate::gauge::EnvGrade`].
554	/// - Values are per-pair picoseconds, each the mean of one
555	///   [`PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS`]-sized timed group.
556	/// - `t_start_s` is seconds from the *warmup* start, a different
557	///   clock from [`BatchSummary::t_start_s`]'s run start — the
558	///   two series describe adjacent phases, not one timeline.
559	#[derive(Debug)]
560	pub struct ProbeSummary {
561	    /// Probe start, seconds from the run's time origin.
562	    pub t_start_s: f64,
563	    /// Timed groups in the probe ([`PROBE_GROUPS`]) — the
564	    /// population behind `floor_q_ps` and `spread_q_ps`.
565	    #[allow(dead_code)]
566	    // OK: the quantiles' sample size, for the qualify-environment
567	    // selftest's table; the grade reads the quantiles themselves,
568	    // and its census population is `pairs`.
569	    pub groups: u64,
570	    /// Robust floor: the [`ENV_FLOOR_Q`] quantile of the probe's
571	    /// per-pair values (ps). The sizing input, and what the
572	    /// environment grade's drift and step signals track.
573	    pub floor_q_ps: u64,
574	    /// The [`ENV_SPREAD_Q`] quantile of the same values (ps) —
575	    /// with the floor, the probe's spread.
576	    pub spread_q_ps: u64,
577	    /// Mean per-pair value (ps).
578	    #[allow(dead_code)]
579	    // OK: the probe's central value, for the qualify-environment
580	    // selftest's table; no environment-grade signal reads it —
581	    // `bursts`, the run grade's only mean-based signal, has no
582	    // environment analog (see [`crate::gauge::EnvGrade`]).
583	    pub mean_ps: f64,
584	    /// Individual timer pairs in the probe — the census
585	    /// population, [`PROBE_GROUPS`] x [`PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS`].
586	    pub pairs: u64,
587	    /// Census: individual pairs above
588	    /// `max(BATCH_OVER_MULT x floor, floor + ENV_OVER_ADD_PS)`.
589	    pub over_pairs: u64,
590	}

592	/// Reusable scratch for the micro-probe, so a probe at every
593	/// batch seam allocates nothing.
594	struct Prober {
595	    /// Per-group mean pair cost (ps), sorted in place.
596	    groups: Vec<u64>,
597	    /// Every individual pair's own reading (ns) — the census
598	    /// population.
599	    pairs: Vec<u32>,
600	}
601	
602	impl Prober {
603	    /// Prober with both buffers sized for one probe.
604	    fn new() -> Self {
605	        Self {
606	            groups: Vec::with_capacity(PROBE_GROUPS),
607	            pairs: Vec::with_capacity(PROBE_GROUPS * PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS),
608	        }
609	    }
610	
611	    /// Run one ~256 µs micro-probe: time [`PROBE_GROUPS`] groups
612	    /// of [`PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS`] back-to-back timer pairs (empty
613	    /// timed intervals) and summarize the per-pair distribution.
614	    ///
615	    /// - `since` anchors [`ProbeSummary::t_start_s`], so every
616	    ///   probe in a run shares one time origin.
617	    /// - The floor is a low quantile, not the minimum: it rejects
618	    ///   one-sided interference (preemption only ever inflates a
619	    ///   group) while staying off the exact edge.
620	    /// - **Two resolutions on purpose.** Floor, spread, drift and
621	    ///   step read *group* means, where the timer's 1 ns quantum
622	    ///   is ~0.06% of a ~1.6 µs group rather than ~4% of a single
623	    ///   pair. The census instead counts *individual* pairs,
624	    ///   because a group mean hides anything smaller than
625	    ///   ~800 ns — an intrusion has to survive being averaged
626	    ///   over 64 pairs to register. A census threshold sits far
627	    ///   above the 1 ns quantum, so counting pairs costs the
628	    ///   census nothing and each pair's reading is already in
629	    ///   hand.
630	    fn probe(&mut self, since: std::time::Instant) -> ProbeSummary {
631	        let t_start_s = since.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / 1e9;
632	        self.groups.clear();
633	        self.pairs.clear();
634	        for _ in 0..PROBE_GROUPS {
635	            let group_start = std::time::Instant::now();
636	            for _ in 0..PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS {
637	                let start = std::time::Instant::now();
638	                self.pairs.push(start.elapsed().as_nanos() as u32);
639	            }
640	            let total_ns = group_start.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64;
641	            self.groups
642	                .push((total_ns * PS_PER_NS / PROBE_GROUP_PAIRS as f64) as u64);
643	        }
644	        self.groups.sort_unstable();
645	
646	        let floor_q_ps = quantile_at(&self.groups, ENV_FLOOR_Q).max(1);
647	        let spread_q_ps = quantile_at(&self.groups, ENV_SPREAD_Q);
648	        let sum: u128 = self.groups.iter().map(|&g| u128::from(g)).sum();
649	        let mean_ps = sum as f64 / self.groups.len() as f64;
650	
651	        let cut_ps = over_floor_cut(floor_q_ps, ENV_OVER_ADD_PS);
652	        let cut_ns = cut_ps as f64 / PS_PER_NS;
653	        let over_pairs = self
654	            .pairs
655	            .iter()
656	            .filter(|&&p| f64::from(p) > cut_ns)
657	            .count() as u64;
658	
659	        ProbeSummary {
660	            t_start_s,
661	            groups: self.groups.len() as u64,
662	            floor_q_ps,
663	            spread_q_ps,
664	            mean_ps,
665	            pairs: self.pairs.len() as u64,
666	            over_pairs,
667	        }
668	    }
669	}

671	/// Value at quantile `q` of an already-sorted slice, clamped to
672	/// the last element. Empty input yields 0.
673	fn quantile_at(sorted: &[u64], q: f64) -> u64 {
674	    if sorted.is_empty() {
675	        return 0;
676	    }
677	    let idx = ((sorted.len() as f64 * q) as usize).min(sorted.len() - 1);
678	    sorted[idx]
679	}

681	/// Census cut for a floor: `max(BATCH_OVER_MULT x floor, floor + add)`
682	/// — the multiplicative rule with an additive guard so a very
683	/// small floor doesn't make every sample "over".
684	fn over_floor_cut(floor_ps: u64, add_ps: u64) -> u64 {
685	    ((floor_ps as f64 * BATCH_OVER_MULT) as u64).max(floor_ps + add_ps)
686	}

688	/// True exactly once per process, for the first run to ask:
689	/// the [`process_warm`] gate.
690	///
691	/// - The state is the warm itself: the P-state boost it wins is
692	///   machine state that every later run in the process inherits,
693	///   so a second warm would pay 1.5 s to re-establish what is
694	///   already true.
695	fn claim_process_warm() -> bool {
696	    static WARMED: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool = std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);
697	    !WARMED.swap(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
698	}

700	/// One warmup pass's length: how long the warm loop steps the bench before it probes and
701	/// re-tests its exit condition.
702	///
703	/// - The two shapes mirror the harness's warms: the process and block warms step wall time,
704	///   checking elapsed every `chunk` steps so a cheap bench doesn't spend the pass inside
705	///   `Instant::now`; the per-run warmup adapts, so a pass is never one sample and never an
706	///   unchecked open loop.
707	enum WarmPass {
708	    /// Wall seconds per pass, elapsed checked every `chunk` steps.
709	    Seconds { s: f64, chunk: usize },
710	    /// At least `min_steps` and at least `min_s` seconds, whichever is larger, cut short at
711	    /// `deadline` (the warm cap), so a pathologically slow bench exits mid-pass with a
712	    /// diagnosis rather than hanging (bugs.md #1). The elapsed-check chunk starts at 1 and
713	    /// doubles to [`WARM_STEP_CHUNK_MAX`], so a cheap bench amortizes the checks out of its
714	    /// measured pass cost while a slow bench is checked every step.
715	    Adaptive {
716	        min_steps: u64,
717	        min_s: f64,
718	        deadline: std::time::Instant,
719	    },
720	}

722	/// The probe series a warm stretch appends to: the prober, the series' time origin, and the
723	/// vec probes land in.
724	struct WarmSeries<'a> {
725	    prober: &'a mut Prober,
726	    origin: std::time::Instant,
727	    probes: &'a mut Vec<ProbeSummary>,
728	}

730	/// The one warm loop every warm in the harness is a policy over: step `bench` in warmup passes,
731	/// probe after each pass when a series is given, and stop when `done` says so.
732	///
733	/// - `done` is tested before each pass with the probe series so far and the number of passes
734	///   completed, so a fixed-count policy counts, a budget policy reads its own clock, and the
735	///   warm-until-stable policy grades the series' trailing window.
736	/// - Probing after the pass rather than before means the first probe already has a pass of warm
737	///   behind it.
738	/// - Returns each pass's per-step wall cost (ns): the sizing input. When a series is given the
739	///   vec is parallel to the probes this call appended, one cost per probe.
740	fn warm_loop<B: Bench>(
741	    bench: &mut B,
742	    pass: WarmPass,
743	    mut series: Option<WarmSeries<'_>>,
744	    mut done: impl FnMut(&[ProbeSummary], u64) -> bool,
745	) -> Vec<f64> {
746	    let mut costs: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
747	    let mut passes: u64 = 0;
748	    loop {
749	        let view: &[ProbeSummary] = series.as_ref().map_or(&[], |ws| ws.probes.as_slice());
750	        if done(view, passes) {
751	            break;
752	        }
753	        let pass_start = std::time::Instant::now();
754	        let mut steps: u64 = 0;
755	        match pass {
756	            WarmPass::Seconds { s, chunk } => {
757	                while pass_start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() < s {
758	                    for _ in 0..chunk {
759	                        black_box(bench.step());
760	                    }
761	                    steps += chunk as u64;
762	                }
763	            }
764	            WarmPass::Adaptive {
765	                min_steps,
766	                min_s,
767	                deadline,
768	            } => {
769	                let mut chunk: u64 = 1;
770	                loop {
771	                    for _ in 0..chunk {
772	                        black_box(bench.step());
773	                    }
774	                    steps += chunk;
775	                    let now = std::time::Instant::now();
776	                    if now >= deadline {
777	                        break;
778	                    }
779	                    let elapsed_s = (now - pass_start).as_secs_f64();
780	                    if steps >= min_steps && elapsed_s >= min_s {
781	                        break;
782	                    }
783	                    // Still early in the pass: this bench is cheap, so widen the
784	                    // chunk to keep the check cost out of the measured pass.
785	                    if chunk < WARM_STEP_CHUNK_MAX && elapsed_s < min_s / 4.0 {
786	                        chunk *= 2;
787	                    }
788	                }
789	            }
790	        }
791	        if steps > 0 {
792	            costs.push(pass_start.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / steps as f64);
793	        }
794	        if let Some(ws) = series.as_mut() {
795	            ws.probes.push(ws.prober.probe(ws.origin));
796	        }
797	        passes += 1;
798	    }
799	    costs
800	}

802	/// How the per-run warm stretch ended: the exit condition's verdict, carried into the report so
803	/// the stopping rule and the printed warmup certificate are one computation.
804	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
805	pub enum WarmExit {
806	    /// The trailing window graded A before the cap: the run started post-ramp by construction.
807	    Settled,
808	    /// The cap elapsed with a gradeable window that never read A (the "run started unstable"
809	    /// signal). The window's actual grade stands in the report.
810	    Unstable,
811	    /// The cap elapsed before a gradeable window existed (a slow bench): the run proceeds
812	    /// uncertified. At the step costs that get here `inner` is 1 and framing is negligible, so
813	    /// the sizing stakes are low.
814	    Uncertified,
815	}
816	
817	/// The warm exit window: the smallest trailing slice of the probe series holding at least
818	/// [`WARM_WINDOW_MIN_PROBES`] probes and spanning at least [`WARM_WINDOW_MIN_SECONDS`]. `None`
819	/// while the series cannot yet satisfy both minimums.
820	///
821	/// - This window is both the exit condition's input and the stretch the reported warmup grade
822	///   is computed over ([`crate::report::env_stretches`]), so exiting on A and printing A are the same
823	///   computation.
824	fn warm_window(probes: &[ProbeSummary]) -> Option<&[ProbeSummary]> {
825	    if probes.len() < WARM_WINDOW_MIN_PROBES {
826	        return None;
827	    }
828	    let end_t = probes.last()?.t_start_s;
829	    let cut = end_t - WARM_WINDOW_MIN_SECONDS;
830	    // First probe at or past the span cutoff; the window must start strictly
831	    // before it to span the minimum.
832	    let past_cut = probes.partition_point(|p| p.t_start_s < cut);
833	    if past_cut == 0 {
834	        return None;
835	    }
836	    let start = (past_cut - 1).min(probes.len() - WARM_WINDOW_MIN_PROBES);
837	    Some(&probes[start..])
838	}

840	/// Whether a probe window grades A on the environment signals: the warm-until-stable exit test.
841	fn window_grades_a(window: &[ProbeSummary]) -> bool {
842	    crate::gauge::EnvGrade::from_probes(window).is_some_and(|g| g.letter == 'A')
843	}
844	
845	/// Classify how a warm stretch ended and the graded tail's probe count, from the final probe
846	/// series and the clock series sampled alongside it: the exit verdict [`warmup_and_probe`]
847	/// records and the report prints.
848	///
849	/// - A window that grades A on timing but whose clock still moved is [`WarmExit::Unstable`]:
850	///   steady is not settled when the box is mid-climb (the measured 7600x dwell).
851	fn classify_warm(
852	    probes: &[ProbeSummary],
853	    clock: &[Option<crate::freq::FreqSample>],
854	) -> (WarmExit, usize) {
855	    match warm_window(probes) {
856	        Some(w) => {
857	            let clock_w = &clock[clock.len().saturating_sub(w.len())..];
858	            let exit = if window_grades_a(w) && crate::freq::clock_stable(clock_w) {
859	                WarmExit::Settled
860	            } else {
861	                WarmExit::Unstable
862	            };
863	            (exit, w.len())
864	        }
865	        None => (WarmExit::Uncertified, probes.len()),
866	    }
867	}

869	/// Step `bench` for `settle_time_s` seconds, appending a micro-probe every
870	/// [`PROCESS_WARM_PROBE_GAP_S`]: the process warm, run once before the first bench of the
871	/// process.
872	///
873	/// - `settle_time_s` is the `--settle-time` budget ([`DEFAULT_SETTLE_TIME_S`] when unset); zero
874	///   skips the warm entirely, which is how a run measures what the warm is worth.
875	/// - Warming with the bench's own steps rather than a synthetic spin means the box is driven by
876	///   the work about to be measured, and costs the run nothing extra: these steps also warm the
877	///   bench's caches and branch predictors, which the warmup passes that follow were already
878	///   doing.
879	/// - The probes (and clock samples) land in the same warmup series as the ones that follow, on
880	///   the same time origin, so the ramp they span is what [`crate::gauge::settle`] reads and
881	///   what the exit window ([`warm_window`]) sits after.
882	fn process_warm<B: Bench>(
883	    bench: &mut B,
884	    prober: &mut Prober,
885	    origin: std::time::Instant,
886	    probes: &mut Vec<ProbeSummary>,
887	    clock: &mut Vec<Option<crate::freq::FreqSample>>,
888	    settle_time_s: f64,
889	) -> Vec<f64> {
890	    warm_loop(
891	        bench,
892	        WarmPass::Seconds {
893	            s: PROCESS_WARM_PROBE_GAP_S,
894	            chunk: PROCESS_WARM_STEP_CHUNK,
895	        },
896	        Some(WarmSeries {
897	            prober,
898	            origin,
899	            probes,
900	        }),
901	        |view, _| {
902	            sample_clock(clock, view.len());
903	            origin.elapsed().as_secs_f64() >= settle_time_s
904	        },
905	    )
906	}
907	
908	/// Keep the clock series parallel to the probe series: one delivered-frequency sample per
909	/// probe, taken at the exit check right after the probe lands. Padding by length (rather than
910	/// pushing blindly) keeps the alignment across the process warm / per-run handoff.
911	fn sample_clock(clock: &mut Vec<Option<crate::freq::FreqSample>>, probes_len: usize) {
912	    while clock.len() < probes_len {
913	        clock.push(crate::freq::avg_freq());
914	    }
915	}
916	
917	/// Everything the warm phase hands the run: the time origin, the probe series and prober, the
918	/// exit verdict with its window, and the sizing input the passes measured.
919	struct Warmed {
920	    /// The origin every timestamp in the run is measured from.
921	    origin: std::time::Instant,
922	    /// The warmup probe series (process warm + per-run passes).
923	    probes: Vec<ProbeSummary>,
924	    /// The prober, to keep sampling with at batch seams.
925	    prober: Prober,
926	    /// How the warm stretch ended.
927	    exit: WarmExit,
928	    /// Probe count of the exit window: the stretch the warmup grade is computed over. The
929	    /// whole series when no window formed ([`WarmExit::Uncertified`]).
930	    tail: usize,
931	    /// Per-step cost (ns): the minimum over the exit window's passes, so sizing reads a
932	    /// post-ramp number by construction.
933	    step_cost_ns: f64,
934	    /// Delivered-clock summary at warm end, when readable.
935	    clock: Option<WarmClock>,
936	    /// When the warm stretch settled and at what clock, scored while the clock series is
937	    /// alive: [`crate::gauge::settle`]'s verdict, carried because the series itself is not.
938	    settle: Option<crate::gauge::Settle>,
939	    /// Wall seconds this run spent warming in total: the process
940	    /// warm when this run ran it, plus the capped per-run
941	    /// stretch.
942	    used_s: f64,
943	    /// This run's total warm allowance: the settle budget when
944	    /// this run ran the process warm, plus the cap.
945	    budget_s: f64,
946	}
947	
948	/// Delivered-clock summary of the warm stretch's end, reported for information and never
949	/// graded: the letter stays a statement about measured time, with the clock explaining it.
950	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
951	pub struct WarmClock {
952	    /// Delivered MHz at the last warm sample.
953	    pub end_mhz: f64,
954	    /// The core's hardware maximum (MHz), when exposed.
955	    pub max_mhz: Option<f64>,
956	}
957	
958	/// Warm the bench until the box reads settled, measuring it the whole way: adaptive warmup
959	/// passes with a micro-probe after each, exiting when the trailing window grades A, or at the
960	/// cap.
961	///
962	/// - The exit condition and the reported warmup grade are one computation: [`warm_window`]
963	///   picks the trailing window, [`window_grades_a`] tests it, and the same window is the graded
964	///   tail in the report ([`crate::report::env_stretches`]). Hitting the cap ([`RunCfg::warm_cap_s`]) reports what the
965	///   window actually scored ([`WarmExit`]), never a silent proceed.
966	/// - The warmup pass is also the sizing pass: each pass's per-step cost is measured, and the
967	///   minimum over the exit window is the [`pick_inner`] step-cost input, so sizing is post-ramp
968	///   by construction and convergence is tested on the number actually consumed. The retired
969	///   estimate phase's open 1,000-step loop is gone with it (bugs.md #1); the cap deadlines
970	///   every pass.
971	/// - Floors, not means, drive the exit (the window grades probe floors), so one preemption
972	///   doesn't fake (in)stability; a warm box exits as soon as the window minimums are met.
973	/// - This is the only workload-independent stretch of the series: nothing but the warmup steps
974	///   has run yet. Once the bench is running, seam probes share the box with it (on a 2t bench,
975	///   with its worker thread), which is a truer picture of the environment the run actually had
976	///   and a slightly less pure measure of the machine alone.
977	/// - The **first** run in the process prepends `settle_time_s` of [`process_warm`] to this
978	///   stretch, so its series spans the box coming up to speed and every later run inherits the
979	///   state that won. Its probes join the same series, so a settled process warm can satisfy the
980	///   exit with few or no per-run passes.
981	fn warmup_and_probe<B: Bench>(bench: &mut B, settle_time_s: f64, warm_cap_s: f64) -> Warmed {
982	    let origin = std::time::Instant::now();
983	    let mut prober = Prober::new();
984	    let mut probes = Vec::with_capacity(WARM_PROBES_CAPACITY);
985	    let mut clock: Vec<Option<crate::freq::FreqSample>> = Vec::new();
986	    let ran_process_warm = settle_time_s > 0.0 && claim_process_warm();
987	    let mut costs = if ran_process_warm {
988	        process_warm(
989	            bench,
990	            &mut prober,
991	            origin,
992	            &mut probes,
993	            &mut clock,
994	            settle_time_s,
995	        )
996	    } else {
997	        Vec::new()
998	    };
999	    let stretch_start = std::time::Instant::now();
1000	    let deadline = stretch_start + std::time::Duration::from_secs_f64(warm_cap_s);
1001	    let run_costs = warm_loop(
1002	        bench,
1003	        WarmPass::Adaptive {
1004	            min_steps: WARM_PASS_MIN_STEPS,
1005	            min_s: WARM_PASS_MIN_SECONDS,
1006	            deadline,
1007	        },
1008	        Some(WarmSeries {
1009	            prober: &mut prober,
1010	            origin,
1011	            probes: &mut probes,
1012	        }),
1013	        |view, _| {
1014	            sample_clock(&mut clock, view.len());
1015	            let settled = warm_window(view).is_some_and(|w| {
1016	                window_grades_a(w) && crate::freq::clock_stable(&clock[clock.len() - w.len()..])
1017	            });
1018	            settled || std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline
1019	        },
1020	    );
1021	    let used_s = origin.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
1022	    let budget_s = if ran_process_warm { settle_time_s } else { 0.0 } + warm_cap_s;
1023	    costs.extend(run_costs);
1024	    let (exit, tail) = classify_warm(&probes, &clock);
1025	    // `costs` is parallel to `probes` (one pass per probe), so the window's
1026	    // passes are its last `tail` entries.
1027	    let step_cost_ns = costs
1028	        .iter()
1029	        .rev()
1030	        .take(tail.max(1))
1031	        .copied()
1032	        .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
1033	    // Defensive: a zero-pass exit needs process-warm probes, so `costs` should never
1034	    // be empty here; 1 ns makes pick_inner frame-dominated, the conservative
1035	    // direction, if it is.
1036	    let step_cost_ns = if step_cost_ns.is_finite() {
1037	        step_cost_ns
1038	    } else {
1039	        1.0
1040	    };
1041	    let clock_summary = clock.iter().rev().flatten().next().map(|f| WarmClock {
1042	        end_mhz: f.khz as f64 / 1000.0,
1043	        max_mhz: crate::freq::max_freq(f.cpu).map(|khz| khz as f64 / 1000.0),
1044	    });
1045	    let settle = crate::gauge::settle(&probes, &clock, tail);
1046	    Warmed {
1047	        origin,
1048	        probes,
1049	        prober,
1050	        exit,
1051	        tail,
1052	        step_cost_ns,
1053	        clock: clock_summary,
1054	        settle,
1055	        used_s,
1056	        budget_s,
1057	    }
1058	}
1059	
1060	/// Size `inner` so per-sample apparatus cost is dominated by workload:
1061	/// `inner ~= RATIO * frame / step`.
1062	///
1063	/// - `frame_ns` is the last warmup probe's floor and `step_cost_ns` the exit window's best
1064	///   pass ([`Warmed::step_cost_ns`]): order-of-magnitude sizing inputs rather than measured
1065	///   constants; the ratio and [`MAX_INNER`] clamp absorb their imprecision.
1066	fn pick_inner(step_cost_ns: f64, frame_ns: f64) -> u64 {
1067	    let target = (FRAMING_DOMINATION_RATIO * frame_ns / step_cost_ns).ceil() as u64;
1068	    target.clamp(1, MAX_INNER)
1069	}
1070	
1071	/// Run a fixed `outer` count of samples, seam-dithered (see
1072	/// [`record_sample`]), through the batch pipeline.
1073	fn run_counted<B: Bench>(
1074	    bench: &mut B,
1075	    pipeline: &mut BatchPipeline,
1076	    outer: u64,
1077	    inner: u64,
1078	) -> f64 {
1079	    let mut dither = Dither::new();
1080	    let run_start = std::time::Instant::now();
1081	    for _ in 0..outer {
1082	        record_sample(bench, inner, pipeline, &mut dither);
1083	    }
1084	    run_start.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / 1e9
1085	}
1086	
1087	/// Run samples until `target_seconds` elapses, seam-dithered (see
1088	/// [`record_sample`]), through the batch pipeline.
1089	fn run_timed<B: Bench>(
1090	    bench: &mut B,
1091	    pipeline: &mut BatchPipeline,
1092	    target_seconds: f64,
1093	    inner: u64,
1094	) -> f64 {
1095	    let mut dither = Dither::new();
1096	    let target_ns = (target_seconds * 1e9) as u128;
1097	    let run_start = std::time::Instant::now();
1098	    loop {
1099	        record_sample(bench, inner, pipeline, &mut dither);
1100	        if run_start.elapsed().as_nanos() >= target_ns {
1101	            break;
1102	        }
1103	    }
1104	    run_start.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / 1e9
1105	}

1108	/// figs, resize disabled — out-of-range samples clamp (see
1109	/// [`record_sample`]) rather than grow the histogram.
1110	fn new_hist() -> Histogram<u64> {
1111	    Histogram::<u64>::new_with_bounds(HIST_LOW_PS, HIST_HIGH_PS, 3).unwrap() // OK: constant bounds
1112	}

1115	/// time axis, which the histogram destroys. Feeds the batch
1116	/// gauge (drift from floor movement, bursts localized to their
1117	/// batch, interference rate from census counts).

1121	    pub t_start_s: f64,
